policy: 151 Atlas sequence remains the shared narrative backbone including Catholic-canon periods missing from four cinematic journeys.
EXACT_REFERENCE qualifies a citation only, not a claim of identical scene, coordinate, historical date or editorial approval.
PASSAGE_OVERLAP_REVIEW_ONLY never merges automatically and carries no location inheritance.
No direct match is not evidence of historical invalidity; cinematic-only episodes remain optional source-review candidates.
Four original 181 group orderings are editorial sequences, not a chronological harmony of all 73 biblical books.
Do not conflate verse-labelled Vulgate, Crampon, Douay and Hebrew/Greek texts without an edition-aware mapping table.
No third-party artwork shipped until licence, attribution, physical crop and source link are explicitly cleared.
Never assert a single date for primeval narratives, or definite road/travel from points drawn on a schematic map.

textualReviewHolds.issue: Joakim/Jechonias succession and deliberate omissions in Matthew's literary genealogy; keep Gospel sequence and do not invent a biologically complete tree.
Luke names a second Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah; Genesis's present Hebrew/Vulgate genealogy follows a direct father-son sequence. Do not merge or delete either in a synthetic genealogy.
Joseph's role toward Christ is putative/legal; Luke 3:23 is qualified in text. No other Joseph ancestor becomes Christ's legal father.
Catholic Greek Esther and Daniel additions have edition-specific numbering; do not map verses automatically between Vulgate, Crampon, Greek and modern English editions.
The 151-milestone source uses a one-verse range instead of Luke 2:21. Normalize display only after a source-owned correction, preserving reference semantics.
